title: Asymmetric grid & fallback strategies for cost, rollout and dashboard surfaces
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem summary: Several console surfaces (cost-insights, rollout config pages, and dashboard tables with inline charts) are brittle under asymmetric viewport changes (split-screen, ultra-wide monitors, touch devices with virtual keyboards). This ticket defines an approach for an asymmetric grid system plus prioritized visual fallback strategies to maintain readability and interaction across browsers and platforms.

Scope: - Grid rules for wide vs narrow breakpoints that can collapse individual cards independently rather than whole-row collapse. - Modal stacking/focus rules for small viewports and for desktop multi-window environments. - Chart render fallbacks: Canvas -> SVG -> Image, and conservative pixel-ratio handling for Safari/Firefox. - Table density modes and progressive disclosure for long rows (cost line items). - Accessibility keyboard/tab order and screenreader-friendly announcements when layout changes.

Out of scope: full redesign of cost UI metrics or backend pagination; deep perf work on chart libraries (that will be a follow-up ENG ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive grid: cards can collapse individually at specified breakpoints without horizontal overflow
Modal stacking: when two modals open, secondary modal becomes full-height sheet on <=420px and constrained center modal on >420px
Chart fallback chain implemented for critical charts: canvas preferred, SVG as fallback, rasterized PNG as final fallback
Tables: density toggle (compact/comfortable) persists per-user and prevents horizontal scroll by truncating low-priority columns behind a toggle
Cross-browser QA checklist items pass: iOS Safari safe-area, Firefox subpixel alignment, Chrome high DPI canvas rendering
Automated visual regression snapshots added for 3 canonical viewport sizes (320x812, 1366x768, 2560x1080)
comments: 2025-03-05 - Aisha Khan: Created ticket after observing three customer reports where the rollout modal caused content shift on iPad split view. Added initial Figma exploration and proposed asymmetric breakpoints.
2025-03-06 - Miguel Ortega: Reviewed initial mocks; asked for a fallback strategy for charts on older GPUs and to document expected trade-offs with raster fallbacks.

2025-03-07 - Priya Nair (Engineering): Flagged potential perf regression when enabling SVG fallbacks for dozens of small inline charts; suggested progressive dehydration and lazy fallback only on failure.
2025-03-09 - Aisha Khan: Updated designs to include per-card collapse affordances and a density toggle for tables. Added keyboard focus patterns for modal transitions. Linked QA checklist.
2025-03-11 - Design review: Held cross-team design review with PM, Eng, and Accessibility; captured feedback below. Preparing small tweaks before handing to ENG for prototype implementation.
review_feedback: PM (Jared Lewis): Prefer explicit collapse controls for cost line items to avoid surprise truncation during billing reviews.
Engineering (Priya Nair): Implement chart fallback lazily: render canvas, detect WebGL or 2D-context failure, then attempt SVG; only rasterize as last resort to reduce memory spikes.
Accessibility (Noemi Ruiz): Ensure ARIA live announcements when layout changes collapse content, and preserve logical DOM order to keep keyboard flow stable.
Design Ops (Samir Patel): Add visual regression targets for ultra-wide (>=2000px) to catch edge-case overlaps with multi-column dashboards.
decision: Adopt asymmetric grid with per-card collapse rules, add explicit collapse affordances for low-priority columns, and implement a lazy chart fallback chain (Canvas -> SVG -> PNG). Modal stacking will adopt a responsive pattern: sheet-on-mobile, centered-constrained-on-desktop. Keyboard ordering preserved using passive DOM reflow rather than absolute reordering.
tradeoffs: Using SVG fallback reduces fidelity of some packed visualizations compared to canvas but improves accessibility and interactivity in older browsers.
Per-card collapse increases layout calculations slightly but avoids global reflows that break adjacent surfaces.
Rasterized PNG fallback increases network/CPU cost on first-failure but keeps UI functional in extreme browser/gpu failure modes.
implementation_notes: Grid: implement CSS grid with named areas and use container queries where available; fallback to breakpoint media queries for older browsers.
Charts: expose a renderQuality flag to the chart component that ENG can toggle per-route to test fallbacks in Canary.
Tables: hide lowest-priority columns behind a 'Show more columns' button; truncation should include tooltip with full value on hover/focus.
Modals: use focus-trap plus aria-modal and apply class modifiers for sheet vs center variants; add z-index management util to avoid stacking collisions.
qa_checklist: Manual test: Open cost-insights with 100+ line items at 3 viewport sizes and verify density toggle persists
Manual test: Trigger rollout canary modal on iPad split view and ensure no layout shift greater than 8px
Browser matrix: Chrome Desktop, Safari Desktop, Safari iOS, Firefox Desktop, Edge
Accessibility: Keyboard-only navigation through cards and modals; screen reader announces layout collapse events
